title: Client-driven stream resync protocol with determinism tokens and partial-function-call resolution
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Clients reconnecting to long-lived streaming responses sometimes receive overlapping or truncated outputs that are hard to reconcile when the stream contains structured function-call events. Existing resume tokens are either too coarse (snapshot-only) or too chatty (per-chunk non-deterministic ids). This creates user-visible duplication or dropped function calls when the client replays or rebinds partial responses.

Goal: Define and implement a client-driven resynchronization protocol that: (1) preserves deterministic replays of previously-observed output where possible; (2) allows safe reconciliation of partially-emitted function-call frames without requiring the client to re-request the entire response; and (3) minimizes server-side state and round-trips.

High-level approach: Introduce a small deterministic token in each chunk header (determinism_token) paired with an optional lightweight manifest snapshot. The token is a cryptographic short hash (8-12 bytes encoded base64url) computed over: the model version + model parameters fingerprint + last-kv-checkpoint-id + a rolling sequence counter for that response. On reconnect the client sends the last determinism_token it observed. Server compares against current stream state and returns one of three responses: 
- MATCH: tokens equal, server resumes sending next chunk (fast-path).
- SNAPSHOT_DELTA: server returns a small manifest describing a minimal set of KV checkpoints or prefix fragments that must be re-sent to rehydrate local caches; then resume.
- DIVERGENCE: token mismatch implies the server can no longer cheaply reconcile; server responds with an explicit fragment re-emit plan or a negotiated rewind point (sequence id) so client can request a bounded re-fetch.

Partial-function-call resolution: When a chunk boundary occurs in the middle of a function call payload, chunks include a semantic marker (func_boundary_hint) and a stable call-id (call_site_id) signed by the server. On reconnect the client includes the last call_site_id it observed. The server will: 
- if it has completed the function call, emit a short confirmation event (CALL_COMPLETE) with the call_id and the final arguments/return id; client can deduplicate.
- if call was partially emitted, server will either re-emit the rest of the call payload (if still available in KV window) or send CALL_ABORT with a reason and a suggested fallback (e.g., re-run function or synthesize best-effort summary).

KV snapshot handoff: For long-running responses that rely on prefix caching, we will emit lightweight snapshot manifests referencing checkpoint ids (not full state blobs). Manifests are small JSONL lines with: checkpoint_id, byte_range_hint, and checksum. This keeps the resume decision stateless for clients that maintain their own caching layer.

Backoff and negotiation: Use an exponential reconnect backoff guided by a new header X-Resume-Policy with values: aggressive | conservative | probe. Clients default to conservative. Servers may include X-Resume-Advisory containing estimated rehydration cost (tokens/ms) to let SDKs choose fallback behavior.

Operator and telemetry plan: Add metrics: resume_attempts, resume_matches, resume_divergences, average_rehydrate_cost, partial_call_reconciliations, and calls_aborted_on_reconnect. Log deltas to the existing streaming dashboard and add a new trace tag determinism_token for correlation.

Trade-offs considered:
- Determinism tokens are intentionally short to avoid large header overhead; risk of collision is mitigated by including model+checkpoint fingerprints and a sequence counter.
- Keeping server state minimal (manifests, not full state blobs) pushes more responsibility to clients and to Dedicated/Private deployments that already maintain KV persistence.
- Partial-function-call re-emission simplifies client logic but complicates runtime cache eviction policies; we add a small soft TTL for fragments to reduce staleness.

Security and privacy: Tokens are non-sensitive hashed digests; manifests contain no customer data beyond checkpoint ids and checksums. We still require an internal security review for the call-site signing method to ensure no leakage of secret keys in headers.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits determinism_token in every streaming chunk header and includes func_boundary_hint when applicable
On reconnect client can present last determinism_token and server returns MATCH|SNAPSHOT_DELTA|DIVERGENCE as defined
Partial function calls are either re-emitted in full or produce a deterministic CALL_ABORT event so SDKs can handle fallback paths
Telemetry for resume outcomes appears in the streaming dashboard and per-route traces carry determinism_token
Conformance tests for collision rate < 1e-9 on synthetic workloads and correctness tests for client replays

test_plan: Unit tests for determinism_token creation and validation (collision simulation)
Integration test: server resumes with MATCH when token intact (end-to-end with SDK)
Chaos test: partition stream, mutate server checkpoint, validate DIVERGENCE path and safe fallback
SDK test: simulate partial function-call boundary and validate CALL_COMPLETE/CALL_ABORT handling and dedupe
